sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case involves a U.S. citizen detained in Iraq. The government claims it must keep him in custody to prevent a foreign trial. The detainee claims he has a right to challenge his detention in federal court.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The government argues that Iraq has sovereign jurisdiction to try the detainee for crimes committed there.
The detainee argues that federal courts have jurisdiction to review his detention under habeas corpus.

paragraphs: This case defines the limits of executive power over citizens abroad. It determines whether federal courts can review detention decisions made to avoid foreign trials. The outcome shapes the balance between national security and individual liberty.
